title: Accessible Computer Science for K-12 Students with Hearing Impairments
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the lack of accessible computer science learning resources for K-12 students with hearing impairments, especially Deaf/Hard of Hearing (D/HH) students who rely on American Sign Language (ASL) and often face barriers with English-based captions and text-heavy materials. The authors argue that existing CS content, tools, and classroom supports are not sufficiently inclusive for D/HH learners, particularly for middle-school students beginning programming.

The paper proposes an early-stage project design for an accessible block-based computer science curriculum and web application. The intervention concept includes ASL video explanations of core programming ideas, captions and transcripts, visual feedback, ASL tooltips for blocks, and robotics-based activities. The curriculum content is aligned to K-12 CS standards and includes concepts such as commands, conditionals, loops, variables, debugging, and object-oriented programming. The project is also designed to support teachers, including hearing teachers, in delivering accessible CS instruction.

The paper is primarily a design and rationale paper rather than an evaluation study. It reports planned future work: producing the ASL videos, then conducting a study with a middle-school deaf population to examine learning impacts. The main conclusion is that accessible, multimodal, ASL-supported block-based CS instruction is needed and promising for D/HH learners, but empirical evidence is not yet presented in this paper.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a design/proposal paper, not a causal comparison study. It reports planned features and future work but no implemented study with measurable outcomes, so it does not meet empirical credibility criteria for blue/green/yellow evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No outcome data are reported, so there is no measurable impact to evaluate. The paper motivates a potentially valuable accessibility intervention, but the broader thesis is unsupported by empirical results in this paper.

interventions.use_case: accessible block-based computer science instruction for K-12 deaf and hard-of-hearing students, with ASL video tutorials, captions, and interactive coding/robotics activities
